unsupported_claims: "a supervised objective is usually more directly aligned with the target labels, while an unsupervised objective may learn more general structure but not necessarily the most task-relevant features"
"In terms of training time complexity, a supervised procedure is typically more expensive because it must process labeled examples and optimize against the target output"

"In terms of predictive accuracy, supervised training usually achieves higher accuracy on the target task, while unsupervised training often yields lower accuracy unless followed by additional task-specific fine-tuning"
rationale: The papers do support the main trade-off between computational efficiency and predictive accuracy, and they support that supervised learning can achieve good accuracy but with high training-time complexity, while unsupervised learning can be computationally efficient and, with a carefully designed objective, match task-specific methods in accuracy.
